title.en: Language work for A Tale of Valour: expressions, over- verbs, c/s pairs and a letter of enquiry

text.en: A story of courage in Kashmir gives us strong expressions about defence, words that begin with over-, pairs of words that differ by one letter, and a way of writing to a place you wish to visit.

keepEnglishTerms: c for nouns, s for verbs
fight to the last man, foil the plan, hold their ground, deliver a blow
what to ask in the letter

text.en:
Some expressions describe action under pressure. To fight to the last man is to fight until every soldier has given his life. To foil a plan is to stop it from working, to hold their ground is to stay in position and fight back even when the enemy is stronger, and to deliver a blow is to strike hard at something.
Use these in your own sentences. A detective can foil a culprit's plan by finding hidden evidence, and hikers can hold their ground in heavy rain by refusing to turn back.
Collective nouns name groups. A squadron is a small unit of about 12 to 24 aircraft with their crews, and a fleet is a group of ships sailing together. A regiment and a battalion are army units of soldiers, so check a dictionary for how they are organised.
Many verbs begin with over-. To overthrow is to take and seize control. To overrun is to invade or occupy an area in large numbers. To overwhelm is to flood or overpower, often emotionally.
Some words differ by one letter, and the letter tells the part of speech. In advice, practice, device and council the letter c shows a noun. In advise, practise, devise and counsel the letter s shows a verb.
So we say 'her advice is helpful' and 'she will advise students', 'daily practice helps' and 'she will practise her lessons'.
A letter of enquiry is a formal letter seeking detailed information, for example about joining a course or visiting a place. Use formal, specific language and a clear layout.
To write to the in-charge of a memorial, ask about the dates available for visits, the duration of the tour, any entry fee, and guidelines for student groups, and end with a polite request for a reply.

problem.en: Fill in the blanks: (a) The teacher's ___ is always helpful and she will ___ students. (b) Soldiers outnumbered by the enemy chose to ___ their ground.

text.en: (a) advice (noun, after 'The teacher's') and advise (verb, after 'will').

why.en: c is for the noun and s for the verb.

text.en: (b) hold their ground, meaning stay in position and fight back.

why.en: Use the expression that means standing firm.

prompt.en: Explain how to tell advice from advise, and list four things a letter of enquiry about a memorial visit should ask.

requiredIdeas.en: advice is a noun with c; advise is a verb with s
Duration of the tour, entry fee and guidelines for student groups

commonMisconceptions.en: Using advice and advise as if they are the same word
Writing the enquiry letter in informal language

points.en: Expressions: fight to the last man, foil a plan, hold their ground, deliver a blow.
overthrow, overrun and overwhelm have different meanings.
c for nouns, s for verbs: advice/advise, practice/practise, device/devise, council/counsel.
